رُبُضٌ [(tropical:) Holding back, through indolence]. رُبُضٌ عَنِ الحَاجَاتِ, (A, K,) in [some of] the copies of the K, erroneously, عَلَى الحاجات, (TA,) and الأَسْفَارِ, (A, TA,) means (tropical:) A man who does not rise to perform needful affairs, (A, K,) and journeys: (A, TA:) or who does not go forth to undertake them. (Lh, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also رَبَضٌ, in three places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
